name: options-boulders-a
prompt: Output ONE image, 16:9. A contact sheet of FOUR separate paintings in a 2 by 2 grid, each the same size, separated by thin plain dark gutters; no labels, no letters, no numbers, no text anywhere. Each painting is a different concept for the same kind of view: the inside of one terrarium room inside a rugged, matte field device, seen straight on from a low eye height, wide, with a soft out-of-focus back and a sharp floor. In every painting the lowest third is a LOW, CALM, OPEN FLOOR running the full width: mostly short even moss or fine soil, plain and quiet, few pebbles, no litter or scree scattered over it, so that small creatures would read clearly on it; a thin dark soil strip along the very bottom edge; two small low foreground pieces sit at the front of the floor, one in the left third and one in the right third, each no taller than a tenth of the picture; all tall planting and every life-support fitting stands BEHIND the floor, in the back two thirds, never on the floor and never along the side edges as a hose or pipe running down a wall. Painted in a warm hand-crafted miniature-diorama finish: fine painterly grain, soft bokeh behind, believable materials, never photographic, never toon, never childish, no cartoon outlines, no toy colours, no gloss, no glow, no chrome, no alien tech, never a box or a cabinet. No creatures, no animals, no figures, no pool or pond, no open water, no cliff, no crag, no ledge. The four concepts must be clearly different from each other in palette, mood, light and fittings. The room is a garden of great rounded boulders, domed all over, never a cliff, ledge or crag. TOP LEFT: sun-warmed sandstone boulders at dry high noon, ochre, rust and sage, hard warm light with short crisp shadows; a matte ceramic heat tile set in the back wall between the boulders and a low slatted vent at the far left of the back. TOP RIGHT: pale limestone boulders with alpine cushion plants and tiny flowers in cool crisp mountain light, white, sage and sky-blue haze; a slender copper thermometer tube and small wind vane on a post at the back right. BOTTOM LEFT: dark rounded basalt boulders with rust-orange lichen and silver succulents, a dusky violet-grey back, warm side light; a matte terracotta heat hood on a short arm above the back centre, unlit. BOTTOM RIGHT: huge river-smoothed pink-grey granite pebbles with moss caps in dappled green light; a bamboo spout dripping onto the moss at the back left.
